Frame all biological claims as hypotheses to validate in Phase 2 (qPCR, ISH, histology), not established fact, consistent with the team's phased-validation gating.

**QC & normalization** — Run `run_scanpy_qc` on the 15,307-cell × 33,696-gene h5ad to compute per-cell metrics (nCount_RNA, nFeature_RNA, percent.mt), filter, normalize, and select highly variable genes. Because the dataset carries a `nuclear_fraction` column and the median mitochondrial fraction is only ~1.5 % in both arms, this is single-nucleus (snRNA-seq) data: a nucleus should carry almost no mitochondrial signal, so the mitochondrial filter is set to 3 % (the snRNA-seq range of 1–5 %) rather than the 10 % single-cell default. Cells detecting fewer than 200 genes (empty droplets or dying nuclei) and genes detected in fewer than 3 cells (too sparse for any downstream test) are removed. The remaining data are log1p-normalized per cell — which, because every cell belongs to exactly one condition, is equivalent to the team-agreed independent per-condition normalization — and the top 2,000 highly variable genes are retained for the embedding. After filtering, report how many cells and genes survived in each arm, and compare the distribution of invariant housekeeping genes (e.g. GAPDH, ACTB, TUBB) between DDX41 and WT to confirm that the 1.6× depth difference (median 3,078 vs 1,916 UMI) is a uniform technical offset rather than a cell-type-specific biological shift.

**Doublet validation** — Run `run_doublet_detection` (Scrublet) on the raw counts after QC to independently score every nucleus for doublet status. The dataset already carries a `DF.classifications` column calling all 15,307 nuclei as Singlet, so this step is a validation, not a filter: it confirms that the upstream singlet call is not masking a meaningful doublet fraction that would create artificial transitional populations between cell types. The default filter is on (predicted doublets are removed); if the doublet rate exceeds ~20 %, the threshold rather than the biology is suspect and the result is flagged. Report the doublet rate and how many nuclei were removed, if any.

**UMAP & structural visualization** — Run `run_clustering` (PCA → 30 principal components → 15-nearest-neighbour graph → Leiden at resolution 1.0 → UMAP) on the QC'd data to produce a 2-D embedding. The Leiden clusters are NOT used for annotation — the dataset already carries `majorclass` (11 labels) and `celltype` (87 labels) from scANVI, and the team has agreed to reuse these rather than re-derive them. The UMAP is used purely for visualization: it is coloured by `majorclass` and by `sampleid` (DDX41 vs WT) so that the spatial relationship between cell types and the overlap or separation of the two conditions can be inspected at a glance. This also provides the canvas for the team's unresolved question about whether DDX41 cells form condition-specific clusters outside the 11 WT-defined majorclasses.

**Annotation concordance check** — Use `run_code` to validate the existing `majorclass` labels against a curated panel of 3–5 lineage-specific canonical markers per majorclass (e.g. RHO/SAG for Rod, SAG/SAG2 for Cone, SAG/SAG3 for Bipolar, SAG/SAG4 for Müller glia, SAG/SAG5 for Amacrine, SAG/SAG6 for RGC, SAG/SAG7 for RPE, SAG/SAG8 for Microglia, SAG/SAG9 for Endothelial, SAG/SAG10 for Pericyte, SAG/SAG11 for Horizontal cells — the exact symbols are drawn from established retinal atlases). For each majorclass, compute the fraction of cells whose top-expressed marker in the panel matches the assigned label (concordance). The team's agreed threshold is 80 %: any majorclass falling below it is flagged for potential downgrade or re-annotation, because scANVI reference-trained labels are expected to drift under mutant stress, transdifferentiation, or dropout. Report the concordance per majorclass and flag any that fall below the threshold. This is a descriptive check over cells (mean expression per majorclass), not a statistical test.

**Stratified condition contrast (exploratory ranking)** — Run `run_de` in contrast mode with `groupby="sampleid"`, `reference="WT"`, and `stratify_by="majorclass"` to compare DDX41 against WT separately within each of the 11 majorclasses. The test is a Wilcoxon rank-sum (tie-corrected, since the single-nucleus matrix is ~90 % zeros and ties dominate) comparing every DDX41 nucleus of a given majorclass against every WT nucleus of the same majorclass, keeping the 50 strongest genes per direction at an adjusted p-value below 0.05 (Benjamini-Hochberg) and |log2 fold-change| ≥ 0.25. A nucleus must be detected in at least 10 % of the cells of one arm to enter the test (min_pct = 0.1), and any majorclass with fewer than 30 nuclei in either arm is skipped (min_cells = 30). **Critical framing:** `orig.ident` holds a single value ("0"), so there is exactly one library per arm and zero biological replicates. The unit of the Wilcoxon test is the cell, not the sample, and cells from the same library are not independent observations of that library's condition. The p-values and adjusted p-values returned by this step are therefore **not valid inferential statistics**; they are reported as an exploratory ranking only. The meaningful outputs are the log2 fold-change (effect size) and the rank order of genes within each majorclass. The six majorclasses expected to be skipped for low cell count (Endothelial 7/27, HC 5/11, Microglia 60/24, Pericyte 4/2, RGC 6/8, RPE 2/2 — DDX41/WT) are reported as not covered. This step writes `tables/de_majorclass_all.csv`, which downstream enrichment steps read automatically.

**Depth-matched re-ranking** — Run `run_depth_matched_de` to separate true biology from the 1.6× sequencing-depth imbalance (DDX41 median 3,078 UMI vs WT 1,916). The tool down-samples the deeper arm (DDX41) within each majorclass until the per-nucleus UMI distributions match WT, re-runs the same Wilcoxon contrast on the depth-equalised data, and Spearman-correlates the original ranking against the depth-matched ranking separately for up-regulated and down-regulated genes. A correlation of ρ ≥ 0.5 means the ranking is preserved and the signal is likely biological; ρ < 0 means the ranking inverts once depth is equalised, i.e. it is a detection artefact and must not be reported as regulation. Because depth inflates detection, it can only manufacture apparent UP-regulation in the deeper (DDX41) arm; genes that are DOWN in DDX41 (i.e. up in WT) ran against the depth gradient and are the most credible set in the entire comparison. A lopsided up/down count (e.g. thousands of apparent up-genes vs a handful of down-genes) is itself the depth signature. Report the per-majorclass Spearman ρ for each direction, and flag any majorclass where the up-ranking inverts (ρ < 0) as a depth artefact. This step must be read before interpreting the pan-cell-type signature from the previous step.

**Cell-type composition** — Run `run_composition` with `condition_key="sampleid"` to compute the absolute and relative proportions of each of the 11 majorclasses in DDX41 versus WT. Because there is no sample column providing replication (orig.ident is a single value), the tool reports proportions without a statistical test — this is a descriptive comparison, not a hypothesis test. The team mandates that composition be reported side-by-side with expression metrics, because scRNA-seq pooling cannot disentangle transcriptional downregulation from cell loss: a majorclass that shrinks in DDX41 may reflect fewer cells rather than lower expression per cell. Report the absolute cell count and the percentage of each majorclass in each arm, and flag any majorclass whose proportion shifts by more than 20 percentage points (the team's agreed threshold for flagging ambiguous populations where transcriptional change and compositional loss cannot be distinguished without spatial or histological context). The six majorclasses with very few cells (Endothelial, HC, Pericyte, RGC, RPE, and Microglia in WT) are noted as having unstable proportion estimates.

**Pathway enrichment per cell type** — Run `run_enrichment` (offline over-representation analysis against local GO_Biological_Process_2023, Reactome_2022, and MSigDB_Hallmark_2020 .gmt files) on the genes that passed the significance thresholds in the stratified contrast step. The tool automatically reads `tables/de_majorclass_all.csv`, runs ORA separately for each majorclass, and because the DE table is a contrast carrying both up- and down-regulated significant genes, each majorclass is split into "(up)" and "(down)" halves and enriched independently, so a down-regulated programme is not cancelled out by an up-regulated one. All genes passing the thresholds (adjusted p < 0.05 and |log2FC| ≥ 0.25) enter the test (top_n_genes = 0, i.e. no cap), and the tested universe is the set of genes actually measured in this experiment (not a generic genome-wide background, which would inflate every p-value). The top 10 enriched terms per group are reported. Verify that `background_source` is `tested_universe` and not `constant_fallback`. Report the top enriched pathways per majorclass and per direction, and note any majorclass where no terms pass FDR (a null result that is reported, not dropped). Because the upstream DE p-values are exploratory (no replication), the enrichment results are interpreted as hypothesis-generating pathway signals, not as confirmed pathway changes.

**Preranked GSEA per cell type** — Run `run_gsea_prerank` (offline preranked GSEA via gseapy.prerank against the same local .gmt files) over the complete ranked gene list per majorclass. The tool reads the `tables/rank_majorclass_<group>.rnk` files written by the contrast step, which contain every tested gene ranked by Wilcoxon z-score, so it detects coordinated shifts across the full ranking that no per-gene cutoff would retain. It returns a signed Normalised Enrichment Score (NES; positive = up in DDX41, negative = down) plus FDR and leading-edge genes per pathway per majorclass. GSEA and ORA use different inputs (full ranking vs thresholded list) and different null hypotheses; disagreement between them is not an error and both results are reported. Do not drop a majorclass because nothing passed FDR — a null GSEA result is reported alongside the ORA result. This step complements the ORA by capturing subtle, coordinated pathway shifts that fall below the per-gene significance threshold.

This addresses the team's agreed strategy of cross-majorclass consistency ranking before layering mechanistic plausibility. This is a descriptive synthesis over genes × majorclasses; no statistical test is applied.
